description: Canonical scoring rules for SpatialBenchRAG eval. Every hyperparameter that materially affects a score lives here; CLI flags exposed by ``benchmark_eval score`` become 'deviations' when they differ from these defaults and are logged alongside the run. Code-side fallback constants must match this file (CI assertion in tests/benchmark_eval/test_spec_drift.py).

numeric.default_delta_ratio_description: Absolute floor for the dimensionless 'ratio' numeric kind (TID 68.1-68.5 shape indices). 0.0 makes the tolerance purely relative, tau = alpha*|y*| (5% at the default alpha), the natural scale-free criterion for a dimensionless ratio spanning several orders of magnitude. The old behaviour routed these to 'count' with delta=1.0, wider than the entire value range.

scale_from_magnitude_buckets.breakpoints_description: Area uses its own magnitude breakpoints (upper_exclusive_area_km2: 2500 / 250000 km^2 = the squares of the linear 50/500 km distance breakpoints) instead of reusing the distance breakpoints, which mislabeled a 953 km^2 area as 'national' and gave it a 100 km^2 (10x too wide) absolute tolerance.

kind_by_unit_suffix.description: Maps a canonicalized unit suffix to the numeric kind used to pick the right default delta. Derived from unit_conversion.groups: distance group → 'distance', area group → 'area'. Anything else falls back to 'count'.

coordinates.separator_description: Character class for the regex parsing a 'lat<sep>lon' string. Includes ',' ';' whitespace and '_' (underscore added 2026-05-05 for TID 111.5).

geometry.polygon_iou_projection_description: EASE-Grid 2.0 Cylindrical (equal-area). Pred and gold polygons are reprojected from EPSG:4326 to this CRS before computing IoU so high-latitude polygons are not artificially compressed along the longitude axis.

polar.angle_tol_description: Bearing tolerance (degrees) for Polar coordinates (angle, distance) scoring (TID 74.1). EM=1 requires the bearing within this window AND the radial distance within the numeric-distance tolerance for its magnitude. The radial half reuses the distance kind's scale-from-magnitude deltas.

grid_cell.description: Spatial-proximity companions (em_spatial / ne_spatial) for grid-cell answer types. The strict exact-ID EM is retained unchanged as the universal `em`; these companions additionally decode both prediction and gold to an H3 cell and score by resolution-agnostic hierarchy containment, crediting a right-place answer that uses a different resolution/encoding. Applied to standalone 'H3 cell index' and the H3 half of 'Composite string (H3+S2)' (TID 48.1). 'S2 cell index' is intentionally excluded — no S2 decoder dependency; strict-ID is the honest measure there. (The former 'MGRS-like grid cell' companion was removed with the 2026-07-22 drop of that answer type.)
grid_cell.composite_h3_containment_description: The Composite H3 half is scored by exact H3 hierarchy containment (the finer cell's ancestor at the coarser cell's resolution equals the coarser cell). Falls back to centroid geodesic distance <= the gold H3 cell's edge length when containment can't be evaluated. The S2 half is not spatially scored (no S2 decoder).

coverage.description: coverage_rate counts only rows that produced a parseable, non-refusal answer matching the declared answer_type — with one exception: correct refusals on false-premise rows (is_true_premise=False with answer=None) count as covered=True since they are the correct response. Refusals on true-premise rows and format errors are excluded. answer_rate / refusal_rate / format_error_rate / gold_missing_rate sum to 1.0.

set_enumeration.description: Strict policy for set_enumeration of dates: any unparseable element marks the entire row as a format error (symmetric with set_enumeration of entities).

dates.description: Day-tolerance for NE on date-typed rows. The rule takes the coarser of pred and gold precision to avoid over-penalizing the model when the gold itself only specifies year or month.

unit_conversion.description: Dimensionally-compatible unit groups. ``em_unit_normalized`` / ``ne_unit_normalized`` convert prediction → gold when both units are in the same group. Never normalize across groups or when either side is unitless / unknown. Factors are multipliers to the canonical unit of the group (km for distance, km^2 for area).
